applicant: a transparency activist, co-convenor of the National Campaign for People's Right to Information
asked: A copy of any independent appraisal or study on which the Commission decided to begin the SIR across the country in 2025, and the files, notings and records on that decision, with time to inspect them.
answer: The Times of India reported that the CPIO pointed to the guidelines of 24 June 2025 and said no further information was available, and The News Minute reported that on first appeal the Commission's Principal Secretary wrote that the Commission had not taken any decision on a nationwide SIR in 2025.

applicant: My Vote, My Right (a coalition of civil society groups)
asked: The definition of 'logical discrepancy' in any official document and the number of notices issued to electors in the 10 States and UTs where the SIR was complete.
answer: The News Minute reported that the Commission said the information was not available with it and might be with the CEOs of the States and UTs.

applicant: a transparency activist, co-convenor of the National Campaign for People's Right to Information
asked: The order or notification for the 2003 intensive revision of Bihar's rolls and the guidelines for that revision, including the forms and documents required.
answer: Deccan Herald and The Times of India reported that the CPIO sent only the link to the 2025 SIR guidelines of 24 June 2025 and gave nothing on the 2003 revision.

asked: All files, notings, correspondence, minutes, presentations and drafts on the SIR ordered on 24 June 2025, and a list of the files recording it.
answer: The Reporters' Collective reported that the Commission replied with a link to a page of 'comprehensive instructions' dated 14 July 2025 that the outlet could not open, and did not name any file on the decision.

asked: Technical documents on the 'logical discrepancy' module in ERONET used for the West Bengal SIR, its logic and parameters, procurement and testing records, file notings, instructions to EROs, and the number of electors flagged under each sub-category.
answer: Deccan Herald (PTI) reported that the Commission held the software questions exempt under Section 8(1)(d), said no module or separate procurement had been made for the West Bengal SIR, and directed the question on flagged electors to the EROs.

authority: Ministry of Law and Justice, transferred to the Election Commission of India
asked: Whether the Commission sought the Law Ministry's legal opinion on the SIR and, if so, the full paper trail of files, correspondence, memos, notes and presentations.
answer: The Reporters' Collective reported that the Ministry said it keeps no record of such advice and transferred the request to the Commission, which replied on 20 August 2025 that it had no information.

authority: CEO Bihar, transferred to the 38 DEOs
asked: How many times EROs sent speed post notices to absent or shifted electors during the SIR, how many replies they received and how many notices came back undelivered.
answer: The Reporters' Collective reported that the CEO sent the application to all 38 district election offices and that after eleven months only the Dulhin Bazar subdivision of Patna and the Hajipur district office had replied, the first saying it sent no speed post notices and the second saying electors were marked from the BLOs' door to door survey.

asked: File notings on the decision to begin the second phase of the SIR and the minutes of all meetings held on it.
answer: The Wire reported that after a first appeal the Commission supplied two pages of file notings showing the proposal initiated by an Under Secretary on 27 October 2025 and approved the same day, and supplied no minutes of meetings.

applicant: a Congress Member of Parliament from West Bengal
asked: Figures on appeals before the SIR appellate tribunals in West Bengal, received, decided, allowed and rejected, district by district.
answer: The Wire reported a 28 page reply, Memo No. 8551/Home (Elec), showing that as of 7 August 2026 the tribunals had received 38,10,620 appeals and decided 82,782, of which 75,443 ended in inclusion and 7,339 in exclusion, with a footnote that the total mixes appeals against inclusion and against exclusion.

applicant: a petitioner in the Calcutta High Court
asked: The circular or notification under which the SIR was carried out in West Bengal and any record the Commission holds on foreign nationals on the roll.
answer: ETV Bharat reported that the CPIO gave no information, that the first appellate authority directed disclosure within seven days and warned on 9 February 2026, and that on 18 March 2026 the Calcutta High Court directed the CPIO to supply the information within seven days.

authority: Election Commission of India, CEO Delhi, CEO West Bengal
asked: The criteria for flagging 'logical discrepancies' and their version history, contracts for ERONET 2.0, ECINET and roll digitisation, Election Commissioners' recorded objections and minutes, data retention and sharing, and State-wise counts of electors excluded, noticed, deleted and restored on appeal.
answer: Internet Freedom Foundation said it had filed the applications and would publish the responses and appeal any refusal.
